text:
Vegas made it close on the scoreboard only when Chicago got lucky. The Blackhawks cut it to 2-3 on a Patrick Kane wrist shot in the third period that carried an 8 percent chance of going in, and Noah Hanifin answered 39 seconds later to restore the cushion. The last blow came at 17:27, when Mark Stone's slap shot, a 79 percent look, sealed the 5-2 win at T-Mobile Arena.

The gap in play was wide and steady. Vegas out-created Chicago in every period, finishing with 4.10 expected goals to 2.01 and 62 shot attempts to 48. In simulated replays of every shot, the Golden Knights win 72 percent of the time. Victor Olofsson opened the scoring on a power-play snap shot in the first, Trevor Connelly tipped in a second before the period ended, and Jack Eichel made it 3-1 in the second with a goal worth 34 percent. Eichel finished with a goal and two assists, and Shea Theodore, who set up two scores, drove the best chance share among the defensemen.

Chicago's goals came from low-percentage looks. Jordan Greenway's second-period wrist shot was a 6 percent chance, and he led the Blackhawks with five shots. Spencer Knight allowed four goals on 3.3 expected, a modest miss behind a team that gave the puck away 22 times. Carter Hart stopped 24 of 26 and was almost exactly as good as the shots he faced.
